set.title: SETTINGS
set.toolsHint: Every turn offers the core set plus 12 goal-related tools. The rest stay reachable through tool_search.
set.ceilingHint: A lower layer can restrict, never widen the daemon’s ceiling.
set.rule.1: Request control before moving the pointer, typing or changing the screen; release it when done.
set.rule.2: An ok does not mean the task worked: verify the real result.
set.rule.3: Prefer accessibility and DOM over a screenshot when they suffice.
set.rule.4: Use ask_human when the decision belongs to a person.
set.rule.5: Answer in the participant’s language; technical names and commands always in English.
set.instrDefault:
# Global instructions

- Create a snapshot before installing packages.
- Work in the visible terminal when people are in the room.
- Never post paths or tokens in the chat.
set.role.efficient: Takes the shortest correct path; allows headless actions when nobody asked to watch them.
set.role.witnessed: Prefers visible terminals and windows so the room sees the work.
set.role.readonly: Only observes, measures and reports; the server blocks any change.
set.role.demo: Witnessed without shell or SSH access, for recorded demos.
set.mem.1: The project staging restarts with `make staging-restart`; it takes ~40 s to answer.
set.mem.2: The smoke suite covers login, room creation and material upload; payment tests are disabled.
set.mem.3: The lab network used a proxy on port 8080 — unconfirmed since the move.

valid.nameChars: These characters are not allowed here:
valid.slugChars: Only lowercase letters, digits, and . _ - and it must start with a letter or a digit. Not allowed:
valid.secretChars: A key has no spaces or line breaks. Not allowed:
valid.control: The text contains invisible control characters. They usually come from pasting — retype it or paste as plain text.
valid.unsafe: This looks like markup or a SQL fragment, which does not belong in this field. Remove:
valid.email: That is not a valid email address.
valid.url: That is not a valid URL. It should look like https://example.com/path
valid.urlScheme: Only http:// and https:// are accepted here.
valid.integer: Digits only, no sign and no decimal point.
valid.traversal: A path cannot contain `..`. Write it out in full.
valid.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
valid.weak: At least 12 characters and three of: lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols.
valid.fixTheseFirst: Fix the fields marked in red before continuing.

tool.screenshot_region: Captures a rectangle of the screen instead of all of it.
tool.read_screen_text: Reads the text visible on screen without relying on accessibility.
tool.find_text: Looks for a string on screen and returns where it is.
tool.ui_tree: The accessibility tree of the active window. Cheaper and more exact than a screenshot.
tool.ui_find: Finds a control by role and name, and returns its reference.
tool.ui_click: Clicks a control by its reference rather than by coordinates.
tool.ui_set_text: Writes text into a field by reference, without simulating keys.
tool.ui_wait_for: Waits for a control to appear or change before going on.
tool.browser_open: Opens Chromium on the room’s desktop.
tool.browser_text: Returns the page’s text without taking a screenshot.
tool.browser_click: Clicks a CSS selector on the page.
tool.browser_type: Types into a page field by selector.
tool.browser_eval: Runs JavaScript in the page. It executes foreign code — hence danger.
tool.mouse_click: A click at absolute coordinates. The last resort when there is no reference.
tool.type_text: Types text wherever the focus is, key by key.
tool.key_combo: Sends a key combination — Ctrl+S, Alt+Tab.
tool.list_windows: The open windows, with their titles and geometry.
tool.activate_window: Brings a window to the front and gives it focus.
tool.wait_for_window: Waits for a window to appear before going on.
tool.terminal_read: Reads what the terminal has printed so far.
tool.shell_exec: Runs a command with no visible terminal. Nothing shows on screen.
tool.run_command: Runs a system command, optionally as root.
tool.read_file: Reads a file from the room’s desktop.
tool.write_file: Writes a file, overwriting if it exists.
tool.install_packages: Installs system packages. A snapshot first is wise.
tool.service_control: Starts, stops or restarts a system service.
tool.snapshot_create: Creates a restore point of the desktop before a large change.
tool.snapshot_restore: Rolls the desktop back to an earlier snapshot.
tool.action_log: The room’s action log — who did what, under which permission.
tool.ssh_connect: Opens an SSH session against an authorised host.
tool.ssh_exec: Runs a command on the connected remote host.
tool.tool_search: Searches the runtime’s 121 tools for the ones a goal needs.
tool.ask_human: Asks a person. For when the decision is not the agent’s to make.
tool.wait: Pauses the flow for a number of milliseconds.
tool.wait_for_idle: Waits for the screen to stop changing before going on.
flow.node.trigger.desc: Where the flow starts: a schedule, a room event, or somebody pressing Run.
flow.node.webhook.desc: Starts the flow when something calls its URL, instead of on a clock. Carries its own path and secret.
flow.node.code.desc: Shapes data between steps. Runs in the orchestrator, never touches the desktop, needs no controls.
flow.node.if.desc: Splits the flow in two on a condition. What follows on yes, and what follows on no.
flow.node.switch.desc: Like the if but with more than two ways out: picks one branch of several.
flow.node.loop.desc: Runs what follows once per item, and leaves when none are left.
flow.node.merge.desc: Joins two branches into one. What follows runs once, whichever way it arrived.
flow.node.try.desc: Goes one way if the previous step worked and another if it threw.
flow.node.wait.desc: Holds the flow for a while before going on. To let something slow catch up.
flow.node.result.desc: Closes a branch and stores its result. A branch may end here and go no further.
flow.searchPlaceholder: Search by what you want to do…
flow.noMatchBody: No node for “{q}”. Try what you want to achieve — “run tests”, “if it fails”, “wait”.
flow.emptyBody: Pick a node on the left. It lands to the right of whatever is selected, already connected.
flow.conditionHint: Evaluated against the previous step’s output. Yes follows the green branch, no the red one.
auto.problem.unreachable: Some nodes are reached by no path — drawn but never run
auto.problem.noTrigger: The flow has no trigger: nothing can start it
tool.record_start: Starts recording the room’s screen to a video.
tool.record_stop: Stops the recording and saves the video as a room material.
flow.notConfigured: Not configured. Open it to say what it does.
flow.noInput: Nothing arrives here: this is where the flow starts.
flow.sampleNote: Sample values from the catalogue, not from a run. Press “Test step” to ask the runtime for a real one.
flow.testedNote: The last test’s reply. Still from the mock: the runtime is not attached yet.
flow.p.noteHint: For whoever reads this flow in six months, which is probably not you.
flow.p.cronHint: Standard five fields: minute, hour, day, month, weekday.
flow.p.expressionHint: Evaluated in the runtime. Below you can see what the references resolve to.
flow.p.switchOnHint: The value that decides which branch it leaves by.
flow.p.casesHint: Each branch is an output of the node.
flow.p.overHint: A list. Each item goes through the “each” branch.
flow.p.maxHint: A hard ceiling so a badly written loop cannot hold the desktop all night.
flow.p.mergeHint: “The first” is right when the branches are alternatives and only one will happen.
flow.p.scriptHint: JavaScript. Receives $prev; whatever it returns goes to the next step. It never touches the desktop.
flow.p.webhookPathHint: The URL becomes /hooks/<path>. Shown in full once you publish.
flow.p.webhookAuthHint: Without a token, anybody who knows the URL can fire the flow.
